calls.head: Where the Flyers have the edge: shots from in close
calls.body: The Flyers are around the middle of the league for shots from in close, and the Bruins are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Bruins keep the Flyers winless
paras: Pavel Zacha opened the scoring for the Bruins midway through the first, and Mason Lohrei made it 2-0 late in the second. The third period was a wild one. Marat Khusnutdinov stretched the lead to 3-0 early in the period. Porter Martone got the Flyers on the board on the power play less than five minutes later. Casey Mittelstadt made it 4-1 for the Bruins less than three minutes later, and Fraser Minten stretched the lead to 5-1 with just over four minutes left. Minten finished with a goal and two assists.
The Bruins carried the play, outshooting the Flyers 32-15, and got the result to match. Jeremy Swayman needed only 14 saves for the Bruins, and Dan Vladař allowed five goals on 32 shots.

Minten and Martone picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Bruins moved to 4-2-0, climbing to third in the Atlantic. The Flyers are still last in the Metropolitan. The Flyers are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-4-2.
